principles.text: When the broader market (e.g. Nasdaq/QQQ) has just recovered from a pullback or correction, that recovery is a good time to shift toward position trading your stocks rather than quick in-and-out trades.

For pullback buys, keep a mental watchlist of strong names and manually watch for price to pull back into a rising key EMA (9/21) or another support level in the coming days, rather than relying on pre-set price alerts.

When waiting to buy a dip in a sector or stock, don't just buy the first move down - wait for a decisive breakdown below a key level (e.g. anchored VWAP) followed by a support reaction or bounce before entering.

A strong rebound off a correction low that reclaims and holds above all key EMAs, combined with outsized trading volume relative to the stock's market cap, signals smart-money/institutional interest and is a bullish setup worth watching.
Trust your stops rather than trying to override or second-guess them with a discretionary read of price action in the moment.

Rather than defining an exit as a daily close below a certain EMA (which forces you to wait for the close), set a hard stop slightly below that EMA - or an equivalent EMA on a lower timeframe (e.g. a 150 EMA on the 60-min chart approximating a daily 21 or 200 EMA) - so the stop can trigger intraday.
An alternative stop-placement approach: place the stop below a recent candle's low, ideally one that also happens to sit slightly below a key EMA, rather than below the EMA alone.

An oversized single position can tie up so much buying power that it blocks you from entering other setups you actually want to take - a reason to be mindful of position sizing relative to available capital.
You will never nail the entry on every opportunity, and there will always be trades you miss entirely - don't dwell on or feel bad about the ones that got away.

The exact EMA/SMA period you use matters less than the fact that you've tested and compared it yourself and have conviction in why you use it - don't blindly copy another trader's indicator settings without doing your own study.
